### 2026-11-08: This session I started the firmware for the chess clock. I’m using Arduino with the ESP32 and the Adafruit SSD1306 library for the two OLED screens. The goal is for it to work like a normal chess cloc

**4h**

This session I started the firmware for the chess clock. I’m using Arduino with the ESP32 and the Adafruit SSD1306 library for the two OLED screens. The goal is for it to work like a normal chess clock (so each player has a key on their side, and pressing it stops your clock and starts the other player’s).

First I matched the pins to my schematic. Both OLEDs have the same I2C address (0x3C), so they can’t share one bus. Also, I put the left screen on Wire (GPIO 4 and 5) and the right screen on Wire1 (GPIO 6 and 7).

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 10.04.12 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/84ba786dc19cf9e333f7f49c1884d84166521d74d81198471c9d559a23acd6b0.png)

Next I added the time controls. There are 9 presets from Bullet 1+0 to Classic 30+0, and the - and + keys cycle through them before a game. There’s also a Custom setting where White and Black can have different times (time odds), and you can pick increment or delay mode. Also, all of the settings are saved with Preferences, so that they stay after the clock turns off.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 10.24.41 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/97f831c8d86a1856e348fb150038b8e9ebecad34bd841812df633eec0273f2fa.png)

The player keys were the most important part, since a chess clock has to be exact. If I only checked the keys in loop(), a press could be missed or counted late while the screens are being redrawn. To fix this, the two player keys use interrupts, and the interrupt saves the exact time of the press. Also, I made it so that any change within 30 ms of a release is ignored as a bounce.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 10.25.10 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/076dcfe5877c4a6a846dd160bf4ddd794df2c121f4b0114293cbe8d9cfa17f57.png)

Then I wrote the clock logic. advanceClock() subtracts the time that passed from the player whose turn it is. In delay mode, the delay runs out before the main time starts going down. When a player drops under 10 seconds the clock double beeps, and when their time hits 0 it beeps for 1.5 seconds and ends the game. endTurn() uses the time from the interrupt instead of the current time and then adds the increment, saves that player’s clock time for the move, and switches turns.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 10.26.34 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/4caa653fa9d6ccbca3eb20ce550bef4c8ab3c0cdd72974250a08995cc74c7ad9.png)

Finally, I set up the Start, -, and + keys. Before a game, Start begins it (Black can also start it by pressing their key), and holding Start opens the settings menu. During a game, Start pauses, and holding it while paused ends the game.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 at 10.29.37 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/21d58cb3470efe0a887ff2519368b29e0418f0b13fb706cbe1502a0fa93a2462.png)

In the next session, I plan on finishing the software part.
